entities.name: Beccaria's "On Crimes and Punishments"
entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: Cesare Beccaria argued that punishment should be proportional, consistent, and aimed at deterrence — not revenge. He opposed torture, the death penalty, and secret trials. His book influenced the US Bill of Rights, the French Declaration of Rights, and every modern criminal justice system.
